answer: An agent’s identity is anchored to an enclave-held key and an attestation that commits to its MRENCLAVE, the hash of its measured code and configuration. A verifier checks the platform’s attestation chain and rejects duplicate hardware identities, so copying a VM cannot reproduce the protected key; creating another accepted identity requires additional attested silicon, not merely a virtual voyage. This makes Sybil attacks costly, though not impossible—a plume of purchased devices can still cross the ledge if enrollment lacks safeguards.
